title: Preserve the Core/Stimulate Progress
coreMove: Separate the enduring principle from the changeable practice, then protect one by changing the other.
sourcePressure: The chapter title supplies the governing duality, and the source says core values and purpose endure beyond individual leaders while progress must still be stimulated.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating preservation and progress as a compromise between old and new, instead of a disciplined separation between core and method.

sourceAnchors.name: preserve the core and stimulate progress
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar supplies the governing duality: keep the core while driving change and progress
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The core is not the old method; it is the reason the method once mattered.

tryThisNow: circle what matters and change one thing

exampleSpecs.domain: emergency dispatch center replacing handwritten call cards while preserving caller-first judgment
exampleSpecs.audience: Olivia, dispatch supervisor managing a system rollout
exampleSpecs.stakes: a software rollout could speed calls while flattening the judgment that saves lives
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia labels the nonnegotiable caller-first questions before approving new screens, then removes old card rituals that no longer protect them
exampleSpecs.firstImage: laminated call cards stacked beside two glowing dispatch monitors

exampleSpecs.domain: heritage bakery moving overnight proofing data from memory to sensors without changing bread standards
exampleSpecs.audience: Marco, production manager trusted by older bakers
exampleSpecs.stakes: quality could drift if the team confuses hand feel with the core promise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco has bakers press dough by hand, match that feel to humidity readings, and retire the notebook only after the standard becomes measurable
exampleSpecs.firstImage: flour stuck to a humidity sensor clipped above a proofing rack

exampleSpecs.domain: nonprofit crisis hotline adding text chat while preserving immediate human presence
exampleSpecs.audience: Sophie, program director reviewing midnight transcripts
exampleSpecs.stakes: young callers may never phone, but chat scripts can become cold triage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 12:42 a.m., Sophie compares chat transcripts to the hotline's presence standard and rewrites escalation prompts without defending the phone as sacred
exampleSpecs.firstImage: midnight chat transcripts printed with time stamps in the margin

exampleSpecs.domain: rural hardware store adding online inventory while preserving neighborly problem-solving
exampleSpecs.audience: Ben, store owner whose father kept everything in his head
exampleSpecs.stakes: online orders can grow revenue but turn staff into pickers instead of problem-solvers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "What problem is the customer trying to solve?" Ben adds that field to every online order before expanding curbside pickup
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a curbside pickup shelf with a paper question clipped to each order

exampleSpecs.domain: architecture firm moving from hand sketches to parametric software while preserving critique discipline
exampleSpecs.audience: Kasia, studio principal training junior designers
exampleSpecs.stakes: speed could replace the slow critique that catches bad buildings early
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kasia reviews a failed design sprint and reinstates red-pencil critique gates inside the new software workflow
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What did the software speed past that the red pencil used to catch?
mustAvoid: software blamed for all shallow work

exampleSpecs.domain: community choir livestreaming services while preserving congregational participation
exampleSpecs.audience: Daniel, music director after attendance splits online and in-person
exampleSpecs.stakes: production quality could turn a participatory choir into a passive broadcast
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Daniel move the camera angle, lyric timing, and rehearsal plan so remote members sing rather than spectate
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a small camera taped to a choir loft rail
mustAvoid: livestream good or bad as the whole argument

skillTargets: separate core principle from inherited practice
choose changes that protect the core
detect when loyalty to a method blocks progress

tryThisNowSpec: Take one rule your team defends. Write the core it was meant to protect, then write one different practice that could protect it better now.
sourceAnchorsNote: Frozen source sidecars for this book expose concept support and source artifacts, but little chapter-level anecdote detail after chapter 1. Use only the anchors listed here; do not invent company histories, named executives, studies, or dates.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
